Question: Who can require you to undergo a breath screening test?
C: A member of the public.
D: A police officer.
Explanation: A police officer can stop any driver at any time and require a breath screening test. You don't need to have done anything wrong first. Doctors, ambulance officers and members of the public can't require one.

Question: If anybody is hurt in a crash, the driver must tell a police officer as soon as possible but within:
C: 48 hours.
D: 60 hours.
Explanation: If anyone is injured in a crash, the driver must tell a police officer as soon as possible, and no later than 24 hours after the crash.

Question: You are driving in a 100 km/h speed area and you see an 'Accident' sign. What speed must you slow down to?
C: 30 km/h.
D: 20 km/h.
Explanation: An 'Accident' sign means there's been a crash ahead. Whatever the speed limit, slow to 20 km/h as you pass the sign and stay at or below 20 km/h until you're past the crash site.

Question: Who may legally require you to give a blood sample?
A: A police officer, an ambulance officer, other crash party.
B: A medical doctor, other crash party, a police officer.
C: A police officer, a medical doctor or an approved person.
D: An ambulance driver, an approved person or a medical doctor.
Explanation: Only a police officer, a medical doctor or another approved person (such as a registered nurse) can require you to give a blood sample. Ambulance officers and the other people involved in a crash can't.

Question: When turning right at a roundabout, you must:
A: Not indicate at any time on the roundabout.
B: Indicate left before entering the roundabout.
C: Indicate right before entering the roundabout.
D: Indicate right when leaving the roundabout.
Explanation: When turning right at a roundabout, signal right as you approach. Then, as you pass the exit before the one you want, switch to a left signal to show you're about to leave.

Question: What must you do before turning left into a driveway?
A: Check the driveway is clear and enter.
B: Signal only if there is a vehicle behind you and enter.
C: Signal for 3 seconds or more and if the driveway is clear, enter.
D: Signal only if another vehicle is coming towards you and enter.
Explanation: Signal for at least 3 seconds before turning into a driveway so others know what you're doing. Then check the driveway and footpath are clear before you enter.

Question: You may stop on a motorway only:
A: To let down or pick up passengers.
C: To make a U-turn.
D: To stop and take a photo.
Explanation: You may stop on a motorway only in an emergency, such as a breakdown. Never stop to pick up or drop off passengers, turn around or take photos.

Question: If you miss your exit on a motorway, you should:
B: Make a U-turn back to the exit.
C: Drive on to the next exit.
D: To stop and flash your lights.
Explanation: If you miss your exit, carry on to the next one and come back. Reversing, making a U-turn or stopping on a motorway is illegal and extremely dangerous.

Question: What must you do when red lights are flashing at a railway level crossing?
A: Drive over the lines as soon as the train has passed.
B: Slow down and then drive over the lines.
C: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
D: Stop and if no train is coming you may drive over the lines.
Explanation: Flashing red lights at a level crossing mean a train is coming. Stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing, even if you can't see the train yet.

Question: When driving on an unlaned road, your vehicle should be positioned:
A: Anywhere, so long as you can see what is coming.
C: Close to the centre of the road.
D: As close to the left side of the road as possible.
Explanation: On a road without marked lanes, keep as close as practical to the left side of the road. This leaves room for oncoming traffic and for vehicles that want to pass.

Question: You must turn your vehicle headlights on when visibility is less than:
C: 140 metres.
D: 160 metres.
Explanation: You must use your headlights whenever you can't clearly see a person or vehicle 100 metres away, such as at night or in fog or heavy rain.

Question: When turning right from a two-laned road into a one-way street that has two lanes, you must turn into the:
C: Lane that has the least vehicles.
D: Lane that gives you the most direct route.
Explanation: When you turn right into a one-way street with two lanes, turn into the right-hand lane, the one closest to you. If you need to, signal and change lanes once you're in the street.

Question: If you are a driver involved in a crash, the FIRST action you should take is to:
A: Stop and place a warning triangle at the side of the road.
B: Drive past at 20 km/h until you pass the site of the crash.
C: Stop and check to see if anyone is hurt.
D: Tell a police officer as soon as possible.
Explanation: After a crash, your first job is to stop and check whether anyone is hurt. Help anyone injured and call 111 if needed, then warn other traffic and report the crash.

Question: If you intend to move your vehicle from the right-hand lane to the left-hand lane, you must first:
A: Move to the left as quickly as possible.
B: Speed up and signal as you move to the left.
C: Signal for at least 3 seconds before moving left.
D: Slow down and signal as you move to the left.
Explanation: Before moving from one lane to another, signal for at least 3 seconds and check your mirrors and blind spot. Only move across when there's a safe gap.

Question: If you are driving in fog, your vehicle should have its:
C: Headlights on high beam.
D: Hazard lights on.
Explanation: In fog, use dipped headlights. High beam reflects off the fog and makes it harder to see, and park lights aren't bright enough for others to see you in time.

Question: What is the best way to check for hazards before reversing your vehicle?
A: Relying only on the outside mirrors.
B: Turning to look over your shoulders.
C: Relying only on the inside mirrors.
D: Walking around the vehicle before reversing.
Explanation: Mirrors, and even a look over your shoulder, can miss a small child or object right behind the vehicle. The safest check is to walk around the vehicle before you get in and reverse.

Question: If you are driving at night with your vehicle headlights on high beam, you MUST dip them when coming up to:
C: A police officer directing traffic.
D: A town or city.
Explanation: You must dip your headlights when you come up to a police officer directing traffic, so you don't dazzle them. You must also dip them for oncoming vehicles and when you're following another vehicle.

Question: What is the least distance of clear road you MUST have in front of you when you have finished passing another vehicle?
C: 80 metres.
D: 100 metres.
Explanation: You need at least 100 metres of clear road in front of you when you finish passing. If you can't see that much clear road, don't pass.

Question: What does a white reflector (cat's eye) placed on the road mean?
A: The left side of the road.
C: No passing.
D: The far right side of the road.
Explanation: White reflectors (cat's eyes) mark the centre line or the lines between lanes. They help you keep your position at night and when it's hard to see.

Question: What does a yellow reflector (cat's eye) placed on the road mean?
A: The left side of the road.
C: No passing.
D: The far right side of the road.
Explanation: Yellow reflectors (cat's eyes) go with yellow no-passing lines. If the yellow line is on your side of the centre line, you must not cross it to pass.

Question: To help you from being blinded by the headlights of an oncoming vehicle, you should:
A: Look to the left-hand side of the road.
B: Look to the right-hand side of the road.
C: Look to the centre of the road.
D: Turn the headlights of your vehicle onto high beam.
Explanation: If you're dazzled by oncoming headlights, look towards the left-hand side of the road and use the edge of the road to guide you until the vehicle has passed. Slow down if you need to.

Question: When passing a horse and rider, you should:
A: Warn the rider by sounding the horn on your vehicle.
B: Slow down and give them as much room as you can.
C: Speed up.
D: Warn the rider by turning your vehicle headlights on.
Explanation: Horses scare easily. Slow down, give the horse and rider as much room as you safely can, and pass quietly. Never sound your horn or rev your engine near a horse.

Question: What rule applies when both vehicles are controlled by a Give Way sign?
C: The passing rule.
D: The 2-second rule.
Explanation: When both vehicles face Give Way signs, the signs don't give either of them priority, so the standard give way rules decide who goes first.

Question: When driving on an unlaned road, you must drive your vehicle on the:
C: Centre of the road.
D: Shoulder of the road.
Explanation: On a road without lanes, you must drive on the left-hand side of the road, keeping as close to the left as is practical.

Question: At night, you MUST always dip the headlights on your vehicle when:
C: Following other vehicles.
D: Driving in the country.
Explanation: You must dip your headlights when you're following another vehicle, so your high beam doesn't dazzle the driver in front through their mirrors. Dip them for oncoming traffic too.

Question: If you have to drive at a slow speed, which may hold up other vehicles, what should you do?
A: Keep as close as you can to the centre of the road.
B: Keep as close as you can to the left side of the road.
C: Make the traffic behind you slow down to the speed that you are driving at.
D: Drive down the middle of the road so that any vehicles behind you can pass on the left.
Explanation: If you're driving slowly, keep as close to the left as you safely can so faster traffic can pass. If a queue builds up behind you, pull over when it's safe and let it go by.

Question: What must you do when you see blue and red flashing lights behind you?
A: Speed up to get out of the way.
B: Slow down and drive on carefully.
C: Slow down and stop.
D: Drive on as usual.
Explanation: Flashing blue and red lights behind you mean the police want you to stop. Slow down, pull over to the left as soon as it's safe, and stop.

Question: How close can you park to an intersection where there are no broken yellow lines painted on the side of the road?
C: 5 metres.
D: 6 metres.
Explanation: Unless signs or markings say otherwise, you must not park within 6 metres of an intersection. Vehicles parked closer block other drivers' view of the intersection.

Question: You must check that there is space for your vehicle on the other side of the line before going over a railway level crossing.
Explanation: True. Never start across a level crossing unless there's room for your whole vehicle on the other side. If traffic is backed up, wait before the crossing so you can't get stuck on the tracks.

Question: The speed limit sign shown, means the:
A: Slowest speed you are allowed to drive on the motorway.
B: Average speed you are allowed to drive in good conditions.
C: Maximum speed you are allowed to drive in good conditions.
D: Fastest speed you are allowed to drive, except when passing.
Explanation: The number in a red circle is the speed limit: the maximum speed allowed, and only when conditions are good. In rain, fog or heavy traffic you should drive slower.

Question: What are you NOT allowed to do when driving on a motorway?
C: Pass other vehicles.
D: Let down or pick up passengers.
Explanation: You must not stop on a motorway to let down or pick up passengers. You may only stop on a motorway in an emergency.

Question: You must NOT park on the right-hand side of the road except when you are:
C: Delivering packages.
D: In a one-way street.
Explanation: You must park on the left side of the road, facing the same way as the traffic. The exception is a one-way street, where you may also park on the right.

Question: If you tow another vehicle, what is the maximum distance allowed between the two vehicles?
C: The length of the vehicle you are driving.
D: The length of the vehicle being towed.
Explanation: When you tow another vehicle, the two vehicles must be no more than 4 metres apart.

Question: When a flock of sheep are coming towards you on a country road, you should:
A: Sound the horn on your vehicle to move them.
B: Slow down or pull over to the side of the road.
C: Turn on your vehicle hazard lights and drive on.
D: Turn on your vehicle headlights and then drive on.
Explanation: Stock can move unpredictably. Slow down or pull over and stop, and let the animals move past you. Follow any directions from the person moving them, and don't sound your horn.

Question: You are waiting at a railway level crossing and the red lights continue to flash after the train has passed. You should:
A: Drive on carefully while the lights are still flashing.
B: Stay stopped until the lights stop flashing.
C: Check both ways and then drive on.
D: Wait for 15 seconds and then drive on.
Explanation: If the lights keep flashing after a train has passed, another train may be coming. Stay stopped until the lights stop flashing.

Question: Can you stop on a bus stop in a private motor vehicle?
C: When dropping off passengers.
D: Only if it is for less than 5 minutes.
Explanation: Bus stops are for buses only. A private vehicle must not stop or park on a bus stop, not even briefly to drop someone off.

Question: For the purpose of applying the give way rule, how should entrance ways in to public areas (car parks) be treated?
C: As intersections.
D: As merging lanes.
Explanation: For the give way rules, entranceways into public areas such as car parks are treated as intersections. Apply the give way rules just as you would at any other intersection.

Question: This sign means the speed for safe and comfortable driving around the curve is 65 km/h.
Explanation: True. The yellow plate under a curve warning sign shows the advisory speed: the safe and comfortable speed for that curve in good conditions. Slow down to it before you reach the bend.

Question: If your vehicle breaks down on a motorway, you should:
C: Lift up the bonnet and boot of your vehicle.
D: Push your vehicle to the nearest off-ramp.
Explanation: If you break down on a motorway, move your vehicle as far to the left as you can and lift the bonnet and boot lid to show that you've broken down. Turn on your hazard lights and call for help.

Question: What rule should you use to judge a safe following distance in wet, frosty or icy conditions if driving a car?
C: The 3-second rule.
D: The 4-second rule.
Explanation: In wet, frosty or icy conditions your stopping distance increases, so double the gap. Stay at least 4 seconds behind the vehicle in front instead of 2.

Question: You are in the left-hand lane at traffic signals. You are waiting to turn left. At which of these traffic signals may you move on?
Explanation: A green arrow lets you go in the direction it points, even when the main light is red. Signal 2 shows a green left arrow, so you may turn left. In signals 1, 3 and 4 the red left arrow tells left-turning traffic to stay stopped.

Question: If yellow traffic signals are flashing it means:
A: That a crash has just happened.
B: The traffic signals are not working, apply the give way rules.
C: Vehicles may only proceed straight ahead and not turn.
D: Emergency vehicles are about to come through.
Explanation: Flashing yellow signals mean the traffic signals aren't working normally. Treat the intersection as uncontrolled: go carefully and apply the give way rules.

Question: You can drive a moped on a car licence.
Explanation: True. A car licence also lets you ride a moped, so you don't need a motorcycle licence for one.

Question: When following a vehicle on a dusty metal (unsealed) road, you should:
A: Keep close to the other vehicles.
B: Drive down the centre of the road.
C: Adjust your speed to suit the conditions.
D: Pass the vehicle in front of you.
Explanation: Dust from vehicles in front can hide oncoming traffic and hazards. Slow down and adjust your speed to suit the conditions, dropping back until you can see clearly.

Question: When passing a bus displaying a School sign that has stopped to let children on or off, you must not drive faster than:
C: 30 km/h.
D: 35 km/h.
Explanation: When a school bus has stopped to let children on or off, you must not go faster than 20 km/h as you pass it, in either direction. Children may run out from in front of or behind the bus.

Question: When driving in foggy weather, you should:
A: Stay close to the vehicle ahead of you.
B: Turn your vehicle headlights onto dip.
C: Use the centre line as a guide.
D: Turn your vehicle park lights on.
Explanation: Use dipped headlights in fog so other road users can see you. High beam reflects back off the fog and makes it harder to see.

Question: You are coming up to a one-lane bridge and you see this sign. What must you do?
A: Give way to any oncoming vehicles.
B: Only give way to any larger oncoming vehicles.
C: Drive straight ahead without stopping.
D: Drive straight ahead but keep to the far left.
Explanation: This sign at a one-lane bridge means you must give way to oncoming vehicles. Wait until the bridge is clear of oncoming traffic before you cross.

Question: What is the purpose of the 2-second rule?
A: When reversing out of a driveway.
B: When following other vehicles at the same speed.
C: When giving way at a pedestrian crossing.
D: When using the indicators on your vehicle.
Explanation: The 2-second rule keeps a safe following distance in good conditions. When the vehicle in front passes a fixed point, it should take you at least 2 seconds to reach the same point.

Question: When coming up to a pedestrian crossing without a raised traffic island, what must you do?
A: Stop and give way to pedestrians on any part of the crossing.
C: Sound the horn on your vehicle to warn pedestrians.
D: Slow down to 30 km/h.
Explanation: At a pedestrian crossing without a raised traffic island, you must stop and give way to pedestrians on any part of the crossing.

Question: When parking downhill on a steep road, the 'Road code' suggests that you should:
A: Leave your keys in the vehicle in case the brakes fail.
B: Turn the front wheels of your vehicle away from the kerb and leave the vehicle in first gear.
C: Turn the front wheels of your vehicle towards the kerb and leave the vehicle in reverse gear.
D: Leave the wheels of your vehicle straight ahead and make sure that the handbrake is on.
Explanation: When parking facing downhill, turn your front wheels towards the kerb, so if the vehicle moves it rolls into the kerb rather than into traffic. Apply the handbrake and leave a manual in reverse gear (an automatic in park).

Question: You are driving downhill on a steep, narrow road and a vehicle is coming up the hill. You should:
A: Pull over to the left and give way to the vehicle coming up the hill.
B: Flash the headlights of your vehicle at the vehicle coming up the hill.
C: Sound the horn of your vehicle to get the vehicle coming up the hill out of the way.
D: Do nothing, the vehicle coming up the hill should give way to you.
Explanation: On a steep, narrow road, the vehicle going downhill should give way to the one coming up, because it's much harder to stop and restart going uphill. Pull over to the left and let it pass.

Question: When may you park your vehicle over a fire hydrant?
A: A mobility card is displayed in the front window.
B: It is not left unattended for less than 10 minutes.
C: There is someone with the vehicle who can move it.
D: If your vehicle breaks down.
Explanation: You must not park over a fire hydrant (fire plug) unless someone stays with the vehicle who can move it straight away if the fire service needs it.

Question: What does this marking mean?
C: Fire hose.
D: Fire hazard.
Explanation: This marking shows where a fire hydrant is. Keep it clear: you must not park over it unless someone stays with your vehicle who can move it.

Question: This sign tells you that you are coming up to a railway level crossing. What should you do?
A: Slow down so that you can look both ways to check that the crossing is clear.
B: Speed up to drive over the crossing as quickly as possible.
C: Stop to check whether the crossing is clear.
D: Turn your vehicle indicators on before driving over the crossing.
Explanation: This sign marks a railway level crossing. Slow down so you can look both ways along the line, and be ready to stop if a train is coming.

Question: You don't have to do anything if your doctor gives you medication as medicine does not affect your driving.
Explanation: False. Some medicines, including ones you buy without a prescription, can make you drowsy or slow your reactions. Ask your doctor or pharmacist whether it's safe to drive, and read the label.

Question: A broken yellow line painted close to the edge of the road means you may stop or park your vehicle there at any time.
Explanation: False. Broken yellow lines near the edge of the road mean no stopping at any time. You must not stop or park there, even briefly.

Question: What does a reflectorised triangle placed on the side of the road mean?
A: There is a pothole in the road.
C: There is flooding on the road.
D: There is a police officer directing traffic.
Explanation: A reflective warning triangle on the roadside means there's a broken-down vehicle or a crash ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop.

Question: You MUST dip the headlights on your vehicle when:
C: Driving on a winding road.
D: You are following other vehicles.
Explanation: You must dip your headlights when you're following another vehicle, so you don't dazzle its driver through their mirrors.

Question: After driving through surface water, you should:
B: Not use the brakes on your vehicle.
C: Brake heavily.
D: Check that the headlights on your vehicle are working.
Explanation: Driving through water can make your brakes wet and much less effective. Afterwards, drive slowly and pump the brakes gently a few times to dry them.

Question: You must turn your vehicle headlights on:
A: 15 minutes after sunset until 15 minutes before sunrise.
B: 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise.
C: 45 minutes after sunset until 45 minutes before sunrise.
D: 1 hour after sunset until 1 hour before sunrise.
Explanation: You must use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, and at any other time you can't see clearly for 100 metres.

Question: The number on this sign shows:
A: The fastest speed to drive around the curve.
B: The speed in the right-hand lane.
C: The safest speed to drive around the curve.
D: The distance to the next intersection.
Explanation: The number under a curve warning sign is the advisory speed: the safest speed to drive around that curve in good conditions.

Question: When coming up to a one-lane bridge, what does this sign indicate?
B: You have the right of way.
C: You must stop.
D: You must slow down.
Explanation: This blue sign at a one-lane bridge means you have the right of way over oncoming vehicles. Still slow down and check the bridge is clear, because an oncoming driver may not give way.

Question: You're coming up to a school crossing and both the School Patrol stop signs are held out. When can you drive on?
A: When both the signs have been pulled in.
B: When there are no pedestrians on the crossing.
C: When the sign on your side of the crossing has been pulled in.
D: When there are no pedestrians on your half of the crossing.
Explanation: When school patrol signs are out, you must stop and stay stopped until both signs have been pulled in, even if nobody is on your half of the crossing.

Question: When can flush medians be used?
C: When waiting to turn right.
D: When parking for 5 minutes only.
Explanation: A flush median (the painted area with diagonal stripes) is a place to wait when you're turning right. You must not use it as a driving lane, for passing or for parking.

Question: A vehicle can use the flush median strip:
A: To move into the traffic flow.
C: As a driving lane.
D: To unload goods or passengers.
Explanation: After turning right out of a side road or driveway, you can wait in the flush median for a gap and then move into the traffic flow. You must not use it as a driving lane.

Question: When must you pull over and allow an ambulance or fire engine to pass?
C: When it is operating its siren or flashing lights.
D: When it is turning right and you have the right of way.
Explanation: When an ambulance or fire engine is using its siren or flashing lights, you must pull over and let it pass as soon as you safely can.

Question: When should you apply the 4-second rule?
A: Never. You should only use the 2-second rule.
B: In wet, frosty or icy road conditions.
C: When passing other vehicles.
D: When waiting for any vehicles coming over a one-way bridge.
Explanation: Use the 4-second rule in wet, frosty or icy conditions. Slippery roads increase your stopping distance, so you need double the normal gap.

Question: What does this sign mean?
A: Vehicles displaying a mobility card may park here.
C: You can park your wheelchair here.
D: Wheelchair parking space for the next 30 metres.
Explanation: This marking shows a mobility parking space. Only vehicles displaying a mobility card may park here.

Question: What do these road markings mean?
A: Turning vehicles should enter turning lane at arrows and avoid striped area.
B: Turning vehicles should avoid all road markings and use the left-hand lane.
C: All vehicles can make a U-turn at these road markings.
D: Vehicles turning right drive straight over all road markings and wait to turn right.
Explanation: These diagonal stripes are a flush median leading into a right-turn bay. Vehicles turning right may drive over the markings into the bay and wait there until it's safe to turn.

Question: What colour is the line painted on a sealed road at a Give Way sign?
C: Grey.
D: Red.
Explanation: The limit line at a Give Way sign is painted white on sealed roads. Slow down, and if you need to stop for traffic, stop behind the line.

Question: When coming up to a Stop sign, where should you stop?
A: With the front wheels of your vehicle on the yellow lines.
B: With the rear wheels of your vehicle on the yellow lines.
C: Where you can see all vehicles coming from all directions.
D: Where you can only see vehicles coming from your right.
Explanation: At a Stop sign you must come to a complete stop where you can see vehicles coming from all directions, then give way to all traffic before you go.

Question: When traffic is merging, what is a good rule to follow?
B: Speed up to make room behind.
C: Let 1 vehicle in from the other lane go first and then go.
D: Let 2 vehicles in and go.
Explanation: Merging works best when drivers take turns, like a zip. Let one vehicle from the other lane in ahead of you, then go yourself.

Question: What is the safest way to carry goods inside a vehicle?
B: On the floor by the driver's feet.
C: On the shelf near the rear window.
D: In a secure place.
Explanation: Loose items can fly forward in a sudden stop or crash and hit you or your passengers. Put goods in the boot or secure them so they can't move.

Question: When should you use the hazard lights on your vehicle?
A: When you are changing a tyre on the side of the road.
B: When you are coming up to an airport.
C: When you are double-parked.
D: When you are in a hurry.
Explanation: Hazard lights warn others that your vehicle is a hazard, for example when you've stopped beside the road to change a tyre. They don't make it okay to double-park or rush.

Question: You must not open the door of your motor vehicle if:
A: You are parked within 10 metres of a bus stop.
B: You are likely to scratch the paint of your vehicle.
C: The car radio in your vehicle is playing loud music.
D: You are likely to hurt any person.
Explanation: You must not open a door if it could hurt someone or get in another road user's way, especially a cyclist. Check your mirror and over your shoulder before you open it.

Question: What does this sign mean?
A: There has been a crash - slow down to 20 km/h when passing this sign until you have passed the crash.
B: There have been crashes here in the past - slow down.
C: There has been a crash - but the road is clear now.
D: There has been a crash - stop immediately.
Explanation: The 'Accident' sign means there's been a crash ahead. Slow to 20 km/h as you pass the sign and stay at that speed until you've passed the crash site.

Question: A white diamond painted on the road means that you are coming up to:
C: A roundabout.
D: An intersection.
Explanation: A white diamond painted on the road warns you that a pedestrian crossing is ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop for pedestrians.

Question: If you are driving and you want to use a cell phone what should you do?
A: Stop in the flush median to answer calls when it is safe to do so.
B: Answer the call at the next set of traffic signals.
C: Slow down to answer the call when it is safe to do so.
D: Pull over and stop to use the cell phone when it is safe to do so.
Explanation: Using a hand-held cell phone while driving is illegal and dangerously distracting. If you need to use your phone, pull over and stop somewhere safe first.

Question: When there are farm animals coming towards you on the road, you should:
A: Sound your vehicle horn loudly until the animals move.
B: Slow down and pull over to the side of the road.
C: Get a passenger to clear a path through the animals.
D: Ask the farmer to move the animals quickly.
Explanation: When farm animals are on the road, slow down and pull over to the side. Let them move past you, follow the farmer's directions and don't sound your horn.

Question: What should you do if the vehicle behind you wishes to pass?
A: Move to the centre so that they cannot pass.
B: Speed up so that they will not need to pass.
C: Move as far to the left of the road as possible.
Explanation: If someone wants to pass, help them do it safely: keep as far to the left as you safely can and don't speed up.

Question: When following another vehicle on a dusty road, you should:
B: Turn your vehicle windscreen wipers on.
C: Stay back from the dust cloud.
D: Turn your vehicle headlights on.
Explanation: A dust cloud hides the vehicle in front and anything coming the other way. Drop back and stay out of the dust until you can see clearly.

Question: What should you do when you come up to a one-lane bridge?
A: Sound your vehicle horn and drive slowly over the bridge.
B: Turn your vehicle headlights on and drive quickly over the bridge.
C: Slow down and check for vehicles that may already be on the bridge before driving on.
D: Drive on and make sure any oncoming vehicles reverse off the bridge.
Explanation: At a one-lane bridge, slow down and check whether any vehicles are already on the bridge or about to cross. Obey the bridge's give way signs before you drive on.

Question: Are you allowed to drive a vehicle towing a trailer with a load that is not tied on properly?
A: Yes, if you drive at less than 20 km/h.
B: Yes, if you put a white flag on the right-hand corner.
C: Yes, if you think it will not come off the trailer.
D: No, not at all.
Explanation: Every load must be secured so it can't move or fall off. Driving with a load that isn't properly tied down is illegal at any speed.

Question: What does this traffic signal mean?
A: Drive on before the signal changes to red.
B: Drive on because the signal will turn green.
C: Stop if you can do so safely.
D: Stop only if traffic is in the way.
Explanation: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You must stop unless you're so close that you can't stop safely.

Question: What does this sign mean?
C: Railway level crossing ahead.
D: Railway museum ahead.
Explanation: The white crossed sign marks a railway level crossing. With a Stop sign underneath, you must stop, look both ways for trains and cross only when you're sure it's clear.

Question: When are you allowed to pass another vehicle?
A: When you are coming up to a blind corner or blind bend.
B: When a vehicle has stopped at a pedestrian crossing.
C: When you can see at least 100 metres of clear road in front of you once you have finished passing.
D: When you are less than 10 metres away from a railway level crossing.
Explanation: You may pass only when it's legal and you'll have at least 100 metres of clear road in front of you once you've finished. Never pass near blind corners, pedestrian crossings or railway crossings.

Question: The bonnet of your vehicle lifts up while you are driving and you cannot see. What should you do?
A: Turn your vehicle headlights on and look out of the side window.
B: Brake smoothly, indicate and move over to the left hand side of the road.
C: Steer your vehicle straight ahead and stop as quickly as you can.
D: Speed up and move to the left side of the road.
Explanation: If the bonnet flies up, stay calm. Brake smoothly, look through the gap under the bonnet or out of the side window, signal and move to the left side of the road to stop.

Question: What does this sign mean?
C: Railway crossing ahead.
D: Railway museum ahead.
Explanation: This yellow warning sign shows that a railway level crossing is ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop.

Question: What must you do when you hear a siren or see red flashing lights from an ambulance or fire engine?
A: Speed up to get out of the way.
C: Pull over and allow it to pass.
D: Keep driving as you were.
Explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights on an ambulance or fire engine, pull over to the side of the road and let it pass as soon as it's safe.

Question: You are turning right at traffic signals showing a red arrow pointing to the right. What should you do?
A: Drive on but give way to all oncoming vehicles.
B: Stop if you are travelling in the direction the arrow is pointing.
C: Drive on straight ahead only if it is safe.
D: Drive on because all oncoming vehicles are stopped.
Explanation: A red arrow applies only to traffic going the way it points. With a red right arrow you must stop if you're turning right, while traffic going straight ahead can go on the green.

Question: Passengers in your vehicle are 15 years or over. Who is responsible for making sure they wear a safety belt?
C: You as the driver of the vehicle.
D: Other passengers in your vehicle.
Explanation: Passengers aged 15 or over are responsible for wearing their own safety belt. The driver is responsible for making sure passengers under 15 are properly restrained.

Question: What does a blue reflector (cat's eye) placed on the road mean?
A: The left side of the road.
C: No passing.
D: Fire hydrant.
Explanation: A blue reflector (cat's eye) on the road marks the position of a fire hydrant beside the road.

Question: What is the closest distance your vehicle may be parked to a vehicle entrance?
C: 1.00 metre.
D: 1.25 metres.
Explanation: You must not park within 1 metre of a vehicle entrance (driveway), so vehicles can get in and out.

Question: You wish to make a right turn on a narrow country road. There is a vehicle coming towards you and traffic behind you. What is the safest option?
A: Wait in the centre of the road and turn when it is clear.
B: Drive straight ahead and do a U-turn when the road is clear.
C: Decide not to turn and drive straight ahead.
D: Move to the left side of the road and turn when the road is clear.
Explanation: Waiting in the middle of a narrow country road to turn right risks being hit from behind. Pull over to the left, let the traffic behind you pass, and turn when the road is clear in both directions.

Question: One or more yellow lights flashing at traffic signals means:
A: Be careful and apply the give way rule.
B: Drive on but increase your speed.
C: Stop until the lights no longer flash.
D: Move to the left-hand side of the road.
Explanation: Flashing yellow signals mean the lights aren't working normally. Slow down, take care and use the give way rules, as you would at an uncontrolled intersection.

Question: When may you park your vehicle on a loading zone?
A: You are loading or unloading people or goods.
B: There is no other vehicle on it.
C: It is between the hours of 12.00 am and 6.00 am.
D: It is between the hours of 6.00 pm and 6.00 am.
Explanation: A loading zone is only for loading or unloading people or goods. You may stop there only while you're actually doing that, and within any time limit shown on the sign.

Question: What must be displayed on the back of a trailer being towed at night?
C: A white flag.
D: A white light.
Explanation: At night a trailer must show a red light at the back so other road users can see it.

Question: Alcohol slows down your reactions when driving.
Explanation: True. Even small amounts of alcohol slow your reactions and affect your judgement, so you take longer to respond to hazards.

Question: What should you do if an ambulance comes up behind you, flashing red lights or sounding its siren?
B: Put your vehicle hazard lights on and drive on at the same speed.
C: Slow down, pull over and allow the ambulance to pass.
D: Flash your vehicle headlights to warn oncoming traffic.
Explanation: When an ambulance comes up behind you with its lights flashing or siren sounding, slow down, pull over to the side of the road and let it pass.

Question: In addition to checking it is safe to move out from the kerb into the traffic flow, what must you do?
A: Accelerate quickly into the traffic flow.
B: Move slowly into a space in the traffic flow.
C: Signal for at least 3 seconds.
D: Reverse away from the kerb.
Explanation: Before you move out from the kerb, check your mirrors and blind spot and signal for at least 3 seconds so other road users know you're moving out. Go only when there's a safe gap.

Question: Before making a lane change to your left, you must signal for at least 3 seconds and what else must you do?
A: Use your vehicle brake lights to warn other road users.
B: Use your vehicle hazard lights to warn other road users.
C: Check your blind spot before moving left.
D: Ensure that there are no oncoming vehicles.
Explanation: Mirrors don't show everything. Before changing lanes, signal for at least 3 seconds and look over your shoulder for any vehicle in your blind spot.

Question: What should you do when another vehicle is following you very closely?
A: Speed up to get further ahead.
C: Flick your vehicle lights and wave your arm.
D: Slow down, move to the left and allow the vehicle to pass.
Explanation: Don't let a tailgater pressure you into speeding up or braking suddenly. Slow down gradually, keep left and let them pass when it's safe.

Question: What is the meaning of a yellow broken line painted on the road near the kerb?
C: You may stop for no more than 5 minutes.
D: No vehicles may stop here.
Explanation: Broken yellow lines painted near the kerb mean no stopping at any time. No vehicle may stop or park there.

Question: You wish to move your vehicle out of a parking space into the traffic flow. What must you do before you move?
A: Flash your vehicle indicators for 1 second.
B: Signal with your vehicle indicators for at least 3 seconds.
C: Turn on your vehicle parking lights.
D: Use your vehicle stop lights.
Explanation: Before pulling out of a parking space, signal for at least 3 seconds to show you're moving into the traffic flow, and check your mirrors and blind spot.

Question: When driving into bright sunlight, you should use sunglasses and your vehicle sun visors for safety. You are also advised to:
A: Turn the headlights of your vehicle on.
B: Drive safely on the far left of the road.
C: Look at and drive close to the centre of the road.
D: Pull over or stop and wait for a few minutes.
Explanation: Strong sunlight can make it almost impossible to see. If sunglasses and visors aren't enough, pull over somewhere safe and wait until you can see properly.

Question: You are driving on a country road at night when your vehicle headlights suddenly go out. What is the safest thing to do?
A: Carry on driving to the nearest garage with your vehicle hazard lights on.
B: Slow down and drive on the far left side of the road.
C: Carry on driving to the nearest garage with your vehicle's interior lights on.
D: Slow down, move off the road gradually, stop and turn your vehicle hazard lights on.
Explanation: If your headlights fail at night, slow down, steer gradually off the road and stop. Turn on your hazard lights so others can see you.

Question: What is the maximum legal speed for a car towing a trailer on the open road?
C: 90 km/h.
Explanation: When a car is towing a trailer, its speed limit is 90 km/h, even where the posted limit is higher.

Question: What should you do when you are coming up to traffic signals and the signals change from green to yellow?
A: Stop at the signals if you can do so safely.
B: Speed up before the light changes to red.
C: Stop even if it means stopping in the middle of the intersection.
D: Turn hard to the left and stop around the corner.
Explanation: When the light changes from green to yellow, stop at the limit line if you can do so safely. Only carry on if you're so close that braking hard would be dangerous.

Question: What is the minimum depth of tread you must have on the tyres of your vehicle?
Explanation: Your tyres must have a tread depth of at least 1.5 mm. Worn tyres grip far less, especially in the wet.

Question: What does this sign mean?
A: Do not drive slower than 50 km/h.
B: Do not drive faster than 50 km/h unless the road is clear.
C: Do not drive faster than 50 km/h.
D: There is a rest area 50 metres ahead.
Explanation: This is a speed limit sign: you must not drive faster than 50 km/h. It's a maximum, not a target.

Question: What is the speed limit for vehicles passing a school bus that has stopped to let children on or off?
C: 40 km/h.
D: 50 km/h.
Explanation: The speed limit for passing a school bus that has stopped to let children on or off is 20 km/h, in either direction.

Question: What must you do if you want to turn right at traffic signals where a green light is showing?
A: Push your way through the vehicles coming towards you.
B: Give way to vehicles coming towards you.
C: Wait until the lights change to red and then turn quickly.
D: Turn at once as the vehicles coming towards you will be stopped.
Explanation: A green light means you can go, but if you're turning right you must give way to oncoming vehicles going straight ahead or turning left. Wait for a safe gap.

Question: You can stop or park your vehicle over a fire hydrant (fire plug) if someone stays with the vehicle who can move it.
Explanation: True. You can stop over a fire hydrant only if someone stays with the vehicle who can move it straight away if the fire service needs access.

Question: What should you do when parking your vehicle next to the kerb when facing down a steep hill?
A: Leave the front wheels of your vehicle straight ahead.
B: Turn the front wheels of your vehicle towards the kerb.
C: Turn the front wheels of your vehicle away from the kerb.
D: Run the front and back wheels of your vehicle hard against the kerb.
Explanation: When parked facing downhill, turn your front wheels towards the kerb. If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll into the kerb instead of out into traffic.

Question: If you are the driver and you hurt somebody in a crash, who must you report it to?
C: A Police Officer within 24 hours.
D: A Police Officer within 1 week.
Explanation: If someone is hurt in a crash, you must tell a police officer as soon as possible and within 24 hours.

Question: When must you signal that you are turning to the right?
B: Signal only if vehicles are coming towards you.
C: Give no signal.
D: Give a right-turn signal for at least 3 seconds.
Explanation: Always signal for at least 3 seconds before turning right, so other road users have time to see your signal and react.

Question: What should you do if you are driving and become sleepy?
A: Drive on the far left side of the road.
B: Move off to the left of the road in a safe place and have a rest.
C: Speed up so that you can get home quickly.
D: Keep on driving but use a lower gear.
Explanation: Fatigue slows your reactions much like alcohol does. If you feel sleepy, pull off the road somewhere safe and rest. Don't try to push on.

Question: What is the speed limit from the time you pass an 'Accident' sign until you are past the crash site?
C: 40 km/h.
D: 50 km/h.
Explanation: After you pass an 'Accident' sign, keep to 20 km/h or less until you've passed the crash site.

Question: What must you do when you come up to a red light showing at traffic signals?
A: Stop and then go on carefully.
B: Go on slowly if no other traffic is coming.
C: Stop only if other vehicles are coming from the right.
D: Stop and wait until it changes to a green light.
Explanation: A red light means stop. Stop at the limit line and wait until the light turns green.

Question: What must you do when you see two red lights flashing outside a fire station?
A: Slow down and drive on carefully if the way is clear.
B: Slow down and stop if any other vehicle is coming.
C: Slow down to 20 km/h.
D: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
Explanation: Two red lights flashing outside a fire station mean fire engines are about to come out. Stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing.

Question: How can small amounts of alcohol affect your driving?
A: You can judge your speed more easily.
C: It will alter your senses.
D: Your driving reactions will be quicker.
Explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol change your senses and judgement. You can feel fine while your vision, coordination and reactions are already affected.

Question: This sign means that:
A: You may stop your vehicle if there are no buses coming.
B: You may stop your vehicle between 6 pm and 8 pm except on Fridays and Saturdays.
C: You may stop your vehicle if someone stays with it.
D: You may not stop your vehicle at any time.
Explanation: This bus stop sign, with its no-parking symbol, means private vehicles may not stop here at any time. The space must be kept clear for buses.

Question: What should you do if the vehicle behind you starts to pass you?
A: Move over to the right so that they cannot pass.
B: Speed up so that they will not need to pass.
C: Signal for them to stay behind you because you think they are going too fast.
D: Move as far to the left side of the road as is safe and do not speed up.
Explanation: When someone is passing you, keep as far left as is safe and don't speed up. Speeding up while someone is passing you is against the law.

Question: What may you do at traffic signals if there is a green arrow pointing to the right and a red light showing at the same time?
C: You must stop until all lights turn green.
D: You may turn left or right.
Explanation: A green arrow means you may go the way it points, even though the main light is red. Here you may turn right, because oncoming traffic is held at a red light.

Question: What does this sign mean?
C: Greasy surface.
D: Left-hand lane closed.
Explanation: This sign shows that the left-hand lane is closed ahead. Merge into the right-hand lane early and safely.

Question: What does this sign mean?
A: You may park your vehicle within the next 40 metres of the sign.
B: You may park your vehicle for no longer than 40 minutes.
C: You may park your vehicle for longer than 40 minutes if someone stays in it.
D: You may not park your vehicle within the next 40 metres of the sign.
Explanation: A 'P40' sign means you may park for up to 40 minutes in the area the arrow points to.

Question: What must you do if glass falls on to the road from your vehicle?
B: Sweep it up straight away if you can do so safely.
C: Sweep it up within 24 hours.
D: Tell a police officer.
Explanation: If glass or anything else that could cause damage falls from your vehicle onto the road, you must remove it straight away if it's safe to do so.

Question: What should you do when following another vehicle in wet conditions?
A: Drive closer to the vehicle so that you can follow in its tracks.
B: Drive with your vehicle handbrake on.
C: Apply the 4-second rule.
D: Apply the 2-second rule.
Explanation: Wet roads mean longer stopping distances, so increase your following distance to at least 4 seconds.

Question: When driving at night, which vehicle lights should you turn on?
C: Interior lights.
D: Hazard lights.
Explanation: At night, drive with your headlights on. Park lights aren't bright enough to drive by, and interior lights make it harder to see outside.

Question: What is the safest way to drive up to intersections?
C: Looking to the left.
D: Use the system of car control.
Explanation: The system of car control is a routine for approaching intersections and other hazards: check your mirrors, signal, position the vehicle, adjust your speed and gear, then look carefully and go when it's safe. Using it every time keeps you prepared.

Question: How close can you park your vehicle to the approach side of a pedestrian crossing where no broken yellow lines have been marked?
C: 4 metres.
D: 3 metres.
Explanation: You must not park within 6 metres of the approach side of a pedestrian crossing, unless markings show otherwise. Parked vehicles there would hide pedestrians from approaching drivers.

Question: When coming up to a roundabout you must give way to all vehicles that will cross your path from your left.
Explanation: False. At a roundabout you give way to all vehicles that will cross your path from your right, not your left.

Question: What does this sign mean?
A: Do not drive slower than 70 km/h.
B: The maximum speed you can travel is 70 km/h.
C: A rest area is 70 metres ahead.
D: Do not stop for the next 70 metres.
Explanation: This is a 70 km/h speed limit sign. 70 km/h is the most you may drive, and you should go slower if conditions require it.

Question: What must you do FIRST of all, if you are the driver involved in a traffic crash?
C: Stop and check if anyone is hurt and give help.
D: Drive on to the nearest garage.
Explanation: If you're involved in a crash, your first priority is to stop, check whether anyone is hurt and help them. Call 111 if anyone is injured, then report the crash.

Question: Who is responsible for making a child under 15 years use a safety belt or a safety seat in a vehicle?
C: The owner of the vehicle.
D: The child.
Explanation: The driver is responsible for making sure every passenger under 15 uses a safety belt or an approved child restraint.

Question: When does a police officer have the power to arrest you?
A: If you fail to supply your correct name and address.
B: If you have no warrant of fitness for your vehicle.
C: If you fail to signal a right turn.
D: If you fail to stop at a Stop sign.
Explanation: If a police officer asks for your name and address and you don't give them, or you give false details, the officer can arrest you.

Question: As the holder of any class of driver licence you must carry your licence with you at all times when driving.
Explanation: True. Whatever class of licence you hold, you must carry it whenever you're driving and show it if a police officer asks.

Question: You are driving on a road with marked lanes and you are in the lane with an arrow showing a left turn only. You must:
C: Turn right.
D: Not signal.
Explanation: In a lane marked with a left-turn arrow you must turn left. Get into the correct lane for your direction well before the intersection.

Question: When may you pass on the left at an intersection, if you can do so safely?
A: When you have the headlights of your vehicle turned on.
B: When the vehicle in front is signalling a left turn.
C: When the vehicle in front is signalling a right turn.
D: When the vehicle in front is going faster than the speed limit.
Explanation: You may pass on the left when the vehicle in front is turning right, as long as there's room to do it safely. Never pass on the left of a vehicle that is turning left.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: No. You're on the continuing road of a T-intersection. The red car is on the road that ends at the T, so it must give way to you.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: Yes. You're on the road that ends at the T-intersection, so you must give way to all traffic on the continuing road, including the red car.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: No. You're going straight along the continuing road. The red car is turning out of the road that ends at the T, so it must give way to you.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: Yes. You're turning out of the road that ends at the T-intersection, so you must give way to the red car on the continuing road.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: Yes. You're turning right and the oncoming red car is going straight. If you're turning, you must give way to all vehicles that aren't turning.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: Yes. Both cars are going straight through an uncontrolled crossroads, and the red car is coming from your right. At a crossroads you give way to traffic from your right.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: No. You're turning left and the oncoming red car is turning right into the same road. A vehicle turning right must give way to an oncoming vehicle that is turning left.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: Yes. You're both turning right from different roads, so the turning rules don't decide who goes first. In that case you give way to the vehicle coming from your right, the red car.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: Yes. You're turning left out of the road that ends at the T-intersection. Even when turning left, you must give way to all traffic on the continuing road.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: No. The red car is on the side road and faces a Stop sign, so it must stop and give way to you on the main road.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: Yes. You're facing a Stop sign on the side road, so you must stop and give way to all traffic on the main road, including the red car.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: No. Both cars are going straight through an uncontrolled crossroads. You're coming from the red car's right, so the red car must give way to you.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: No. The red car faces a Stop sign, so it must stop and give way to you. There's no sign on your road.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: No. You're going straight, and the red car is turning right across your path. Turning traffic must give way to traffic that isn't turning.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: Yes. You're turning right and the red car is going straight. If you're turning, you must give way to all vehicles that aren't turning.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: Yes. Both cars are going straight through an uncontrolled crossroads, and the red car is coming from your right, so you must give way to it.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: No. Both cars are going straight through an uncontrolled crossroads. You're coming from the red car's right, so the red car must give way to you.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: No. The red car faces a Give Way sign, so it must give way to you on the main road.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: No. The motorcyclist is turning out of the side road while you're going straight. Turning traffic must give way to traffic that isn't turning.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: Yes. You're facing a Give Way sign, so you must give way to all traffic on the main road, including the red car.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: Yes. You're facing a Stop sign. Stop completely, then give way to all traffic on the main road, including the red car.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: No. The red car is coming out of a driveway, and a driver leaving a driveway must give way to all road users. You don't need to give way to it.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: Yes. A green light lets you go, but when you're turning right you must give way to oncoming traffic going straight or turning left, like the red car.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: No. The red car's signal is red, so it must stop. Your green light lets you carry on straight through.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: Yes. The red car has a green light, so your signal is red. You must stop and wait for it to change.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: No. You have a green light and you're going straight. The red car's signal is red, so it must stop.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: No. The green right-turn arrow means oncoming traffic is held at a red light, so you can turn right without giving way to it.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: Yes. At a roundabout you give way to all vehicles that will cross your path from your right. The red car is coming from your right, so let it go first.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: No. At a roundabout you give way only to vehicles coming from your right. The red car is on your left, so it must give way to you.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: Yes. The main road bends to the left. Carrying on into the side road means leaving the main road, which counts as turning across the yellow car's path. Turning traffic gives way to traffic that isn't turning.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: Yes. At a roundabout you give way to all vehicles that will cross your path from your right. The red car is coming from your right, so you give way.

Question: Does the driver of the blue car have to give way?
Explanation: No. At a roundabout you give way only to traffic coming from your right. The red car is on your left, so it must give way to you.

Question: You are the driver of the blue car. Of the 4 hazards marked, which one is most likely to require you to take urgent action?
C: The oncoming car.
D: The pedestrian.
Explanation: The cyclist is right in front of you and about to reach the parked car. They'll probably swing out into your path to get around it, so slow down and give them room.

Question: You are the driver of the blue car. Of the 4 hazards marked, which one is most likely to require you to take urgent action?
A: The car parked on the left.
C: The oncoming car.
D: The car parked on the right.
Explanation: The car reversing out of the parking space is moving into your path, and its driver may not have seen you. Be ready to slow down or stop.

Question: You are the driver of the blue car. Of the 4 hazards marked, which one is most likely to require you to take urgent action?
C: The grey car ahead of you.
D: The green car turning right.
Explanation: The green car is about to turn right across your lane. It should give way to you, but if its driver misjudges the gap you'll have to react immediately, so watch it closely.

Question: You are the driver of the blue car. Of the 4 hazards marked, which one is most likely to require you to take urgent action?
C: The grey parked car.
D: The red parked car.
Explanation: Children can be unpredictable and may step out without looking. The child near the parked cars is the most likely to move into your path, so slow down and be ready to stop.

Question: A vehicle should not send out visible smoke for more than:
C: 8 seconds.
D: 10 seconds.
Explanation: Your vehicle must not give off visible smoke for more than 10 seconds at a time. Continuous smoke points to an engine problem and is a hazard to others.

Question: You look in the mirror and see a cyclist. What should you do when opening the car door?
A: Check you won't cause a hazard to the cyclist.
B: Wait for the cyclist to move before opening the door.
C: Warn the cyclist by sounding the horn.
D: Expect the cyclist to swerve.
Explanation: Opening your door into a cyclist's path can cause a serious crash. Check your mirror and over your shoulder, and wait until the cyclist has passed before you open the door.

Question: You wish to turn left at the intersection. Do you:
A: Speed up and turn in front of the cyclist.
B: Sound the warning device to warn the cyclist.
C: Stay back until the cyclist has passed the intersection.
D: Keep driving to the next intersection.
Explanation: Never cut across a cyclist when turning left. Stay behind them until they've passed the intersection, then make your turn.

Question: You see a pedestrian carrying a white cane crossing the road. What should you do?
A: Rev the engine to let them know that you are waiting.
B: Take extra care and allow them to cross the road in their own time.
C: Turn on the vehicle hazard lights and drive on.
D: Speed up and pass in front of them.
Explanation: A white cane means the person is blind or has low vision. Take extra care, stay stopped and let them cross in their own time. Don't rev your engine or sound your horn.

Question: The 'speed limit' means the:
A: Slowest speed you can drive in good conditions.
B: Average speed you can drive in good conditions.
C: Maximum legal speed you can drive in good conditions.
D: Fastest speed you can drive, except when overtaking.
Explanation: The speed limit is the maximum legal speed, and only in good conditions. When it's wet, dark, foggy or busy, drive slower.

Question: You are driving past a line of parked cars. You notice a ball bouncing out into the road ahead. What should you do?
A: Keep driving at the same speed.
B: Keep driving at the same speed and flash the vehicle's headlights.
C: Slow down and be prepared to stop for children.
D: Slow down and move to the right-hand side of the road.
Explanation: A ball bouncing into the road often means a child is about to run after it. Slow down and be ready to stop.

Question: You are the driver of the blue car. What should you do?
A: Keep driving as the cyclist has to stop.
B: Stop and give way to the cyclist.
C: Keep driving as the cyclist has to give way to larger vehicles.
D: Sound the warning device to warn the cyclist.
Explanation: You're facing a Give Way sign, so you must give way to all traffic on the road you're entering, and that includes cyclists. Stop if you need to and let the cyclist go first.

Question: You are the driver of the blue car. What must you do?
A: Speed up to get around in front of the cyclist.
B: Keep driving as the cyclist has to give way to larger vehicles.
C: Sound the warning device to warn the cyclist.
D: Stop and give way to the cyclist.
Explanation: You're on the road that ends at the T-intersection, so you must give way to all traffic on the continuing road, including the cyclist. Cyclists have the same rights as other vehicles.

Question: When driving at night on a road with lanes you must be able to stop in half the length of clear road you can see in front of you.
Explanation: False. On a road with marked lanes, you must be able to stop within the length of clear road you can see. You need to stop within half that distance on roads without a centre line, where you may have to share the space with oncoming traffic.

Question: If you are turning left at an intersection, you must give way to vehicles coming towards you that are turning right.
Explanation: False. A vehicle turning right must give way to an oncoming vehicle that's turning left. If you're the one turning left, the oncoming right-turner gives way to you.

Question: When going 'straight' through a roundabout, don't signal as you approach the roundabout, only signal left as you pass the exit before the one you want.
Explanation: True. When you're going straight through a roundabout, don't signal on the approach. Signal left as you pass the exit before the one you're taking, so others know you're leaving.

Question: You may use a right turn bay to overtake a vehicle travelling straight ahead.
Explanation: False. A right-turn bay is only for vehicles waiting to turn right. You must not use it to overtake.

Question: You can be fined if your vehicle is on a road and not up to warrant of fitness standard.
Explanation: True. Your vehicle must be kept up to warrant of fitness standard at all times, not just on inspection day. You can be fined if it isn't.

Question: When coming up to a pedestrian crossing with a raised traffic island, what must you do?
A: Stop and give way to pedestrians on any part of the crossing.
B: Keep going because the pedestrian will stop on the raised island.
C: Stop and give way to pedestrians on your half of the road.
D: Slow down until the pedestrian is on the raised island then drive on.
Explanation: When a pedestrian crossing is split by a raised traffic island, each half works as a separate crossing. Stop and give way to pedestrians on your half of the road.

Question: What does the legal definition of a road include?
B: One way streets and cycle lanes.
C: Public roads, highways, footpaths and car parks.
D: Streets, highways, and any place the public has access to such as bridges, beaches, car parks etc.
Explanation: Legally, a 'road' includes streets, highways and any place the public has access to, such as bridges, beaches and car parks. The road rules, including drink-driving laws, apply in all of them.

Question: At an intersection what do a police officer's directions overrule?
C: The give way rules.
D: Traffic signals, road signs, the give way rules.
Explanation: A police officer's directions override traffic signals, road signs and the give way rules. Always do what the officer tells you.

Question: What must you do at an intersection controlled by a stop sign?
A: Stop where you can see all vehicles coming from your right.
B: Slow down and drive on if no vehicles are coming.
C: Give way to all vehicles on your left.
D: Come to a complete stop where you can see vehicles coming from all directions.
Explanation: At a Stop sign you must come to a complete stop where you can see vehicles coming from all directions, then give way to all traffic before you go.

Question: What must you do at an intersection controlled by a Give Way sign?
A: Give way to all vehicles, including those on a stop sign.
C: Give way to all vehicles, except those on a stop sign.
D: Give way to all vehicles on your right.
Explanation: At a Give Way sign you must give way to all vehicles, except those facing a Stop sign. Drivers at a Stop sign must give way to you.

Question: What is the recommended distance you should allow when driving past a cyclist?
C: 2 metres.
D: 2.5 metres.
Explanation: Leave at least 1.5 metres between your vehicle and a cyclist when you pass. If there isn't room, slow down and wait behind until it's safe to pass.

Question: What is the maximum distance a load may overhang your vehicle behind the rear axle?
C: 3 metres.
D: 2.5 metres.
Explanation: A load must not stick out more than 4 metres behind the rear axle of your vehicle.

Question: Your vehicle has a current warrant of fitness but a rear red stop light is not working. What should you do?
A: Get it fixed before your next warrant is due.
B: Your vehicle still has a warrant of fitness so you don't need to do anything.
C: Fix it immediately because you could get a fine.
D: Stop driving your vehicle until it is fixed.
Explanation: Your vehicle must be roadworthy at all times, not just on the day of its WoF inspection. A broken stop light is unsafe and could earn you a fine, so get it fixed straight away.

Question: What does a warrant of fitness show?
A: The vehicle was inspected by an approved WoF inspector and was roadworthy when last inspected.
B: The vehicle failed the WoF inspection and you have 28 days to fix the vehicle.
C: Your commercial vehicle has been inspected and is roadworthy.
D: The vehicle was inspected by an approved WoF inspector but is not considered roadworthy.
Explanation: A warrant of fitness shows the vehicle met the safety standards when it was last inspected by an approved WoF inspector. It's up to you to keep it in that condition between inspections.

Question: Which person can legally stop and do a roadside check of your vehicle?
C: A police officer.
D: A lawyer.
Explanation: A police officer can stop you and carry out a roadside check of your vehicle at any time.

Question: If your vehicle was first registered less than six years ago, when does it require a warrant of fitness inspection?
C: Every 8 months.
D: Every 6 months.
Explanation: Newer vehicles need a warrant of fitness inspection every 12 months. Older vehicles need to be checked more often.

Question: Where should the warrant of fitness label for your car be displayed?
A: Inside the windscreen, in the top left-hand corner (as viewed from the driver's seat).
B: Inside the windscreen, in the top right-hand corner (as viewed from the driver's seat).
C: Inside the windscreen, in the bottom right-hand corner (as viewed from the driver's seat).
D: Inside the windscreen, in the bottom left-hand corner (as viewed from the driver's seat).
Explanation: The WoF label goes on the inside of the windscreen on the same side as the steering wheel, so in the top right-hand corner as seen from the driver's seat.

Question: What is the maximum distance a load may extend in front of a car?
A: 2 metres forward of the front edge of the front seat.
B: 4 metres forward of the front edge of the front seat.
C: 3 metres forward of the front edge of the front seat.
D: 2.5 metres forward of the front edge of the front seat.
Explanation: A load must not stick out more than 3 metres in front of the front edge of the front seat.

Question: Which parts of the car must be in good condition to prevent too much noise and gases entering the car?
C: The doors and windows.
D: The silencer and engine.
Explanation: A faulty engine or exhaust can let noise and poisonous gases like carbon monoxide into the car. Keep the engine and exhaust system in good condition.

Question: At night, what must a towed vehicle have at the back of it?
C: A white light.
D: A red light.
Explanation: At night a towed vehicle must show a red light at the back so following traffic can see it.

Question: What should you do before any modification is carried out on your vehicle?
A: Ask a mechanic to check whether the modifications are safe.
B: If you're only fitting extra lights you don't need to do anything.
C: Make sure a trained professional is carrying out the modifications.
D: Check with an approved WoF inspector that the modifications are legal.
Explanation: Some modifications make a vehicle illegal or unsafe. Before you modify your vehicle, check with an approved WoF inspector that the changes are legal.

Question: To tow a trailer on a full car licence, the weight of your vehicle plus the weight of the trailer must not exceed what weight?
A: 6000 kg (including the load you are carrying).
B: 4500 kg (excluding the load you are carrying).
C: 4000 kg (including the load you are carrying).
D: 5000 kg (including the load you are carrying).
Explanation: On a full car licence you can tow as long as the combined weight of your vehicle and trailer, including their loads, is no more than 6000 kg.

Question: If you have had a flat tyre and have fitted a 'space saver wheel' what must you do?
A: Make sure the space-saver tyre is inflated to normal tyre pressure.
B: Drive for a short distance only and not faster than 80 km/h.
C: Drive as far as you like but not faster than 80 km/h.
D: Drive for a short distance only and not faster than 100 km/h.
Explanation: A space-saver wheel is a temporary spare. Drive on it only for a short distance, such as to get your tyre fixed, and no faster than 80 km/h.

Question: What is the maximum speed you may drive if you have a 'space saver wheel' fitted?
B: 100 km/h so you don't hold up other traffic.
C: 80 km/h. If the space-saver wheel displays a lower speed that speed applies.
D: 90 km/h.
Explanation: Space-saver wheels aren't built for normal driving. Keep to 80 km/h or less, or to the lower speed shown on the wheel if there is one.

Question: If you have a restricted licence when can you carry passengers?
A: One of your passengers has their full licence.
C: Between the hours of 10 pm and 5 am.
D: When a supervisor, who has held a NZ car licence for at least 2 years, is in the front seat.
Explanation: On a restricted licence you can't carry passengers unless a supervisor sits in the front passenger seat. A supervisor must have held a full NZ car licence for at least 2 years. There are limited exceptions, such as carrying your partner or dependants.

Question: If you have a learner licence can you carry passengers?
A: Yes, provided your supervisor agrees and is sitting in the front passenger seat.
B: Yes, provided you're with a supervisor and it's between the hours of 5 am and 10 pm.
C: No, you can only drive with a supervisor.
D: Yes, provided you're with a supervisor and you have no more than 2 passengers.
Explanation: Learner drivers must always have a supervisor in the front passenger seat. You can carry other passengers as long as your supervisor agrees.

Question: When you have a learner licence you must always drive with a supervisor. What is a supervisor?
A: An adult that sits next to you in the passenger seat.
B: Someone that has held a valid full NZ licence for at least 2 years and sits in the passenger seat.
C: Anyone in the car that has held a valid full NZ licence for at least 2 years.
D: Someone who sits in the passenger seat with a restricted NZ licence.
Explanation: A supervisor must have held a full NZ licence for at least 2 years and must sit in the front passenger seat beside you.

Question: When you have a learner licence do you have to have it with you when you drive?
A: No, your supervisor will carry their licence because they're responsible for the car.
B: Only when you're driving at night.
C: Yes, you must have your learner licence with you whenever you are driving.
D: Only when you are carrying passengers as well as your supervisor.
Explanation: You must carry your learner licence whenever you're driving. Every driver must carry their licence while driving.

Question: A police officer can impound your car on the spot if you are caught driving while disqualified.
Explanation: True. If you're caught driving while disqualified, the police can impound your vehicle on the spot.

Question: If you are under 20 years of age the legal alcohol limit is zero. What does this mean?
A: One drink could see you charged with drink driving.
B: You could face a fine and 50 demerit points if your alcohol level is less than 150 micrograms per litre of breath.
C: You could be disqualified from driving, given demerits, fined or imprisoned if your alcohol level is higher than 150 micrograms per litre of breath.
D: All of the above.
Explanation: For drivers under 20 the alcohol limit is zero, so even one drink could put you over. Up to 150 micrograms per litre of breath means a fine and 50 demerit points; above that you can be disqualified, fined or imprisoned.

Question: What lights should you use if your vehicle has broken down and is being towed?
C: Hazard lights.
D: Left hand indicator.
Explanation: A broken-down vehicle being towed should use its hazard lights to warn other road users that it isn't moving under its own power.

Question: You are driving and you see an accident sign. What speed must you slow down to?
C: 80 km/h
D: 20 km/h
Explanation: When you see an 'Accident' sign, slow to 20 km/h and stay at or below that speed until you've passed the crash.

Question: What does this sign mean?
C: Open speed limit applies dependent on conditions, maximum speed of 100 km/h.
D: Accident.
Explanation: This sign means the open road speed limit applies from here: a maximum of 100 km/h. You must still drive to suit the conditions.

Question: On a transit lane what does T2 mean?
A: You can only use a bicycle or motorcycle in this lane.
B: Buses only may use this lane.
C: Vehicles with 2 or more passengers, buses, bicycles and motorcycles may use this lane.
D: Taxis only may use this lane.
Explanation: A T2 transit lane can be used only by vehicles carrying at least 2 people (the driver counts), plus buses, motorcycles and cyclists.

Question: What does this sign mean?
C: Wash your car today.
D: Use wipers to prevent broken windshield.
Explanation: This warning sign means there's loose gravel or chip on the road ahead. Slow down: loose stones reduce grip and can be flicked up at other vehicles.

Question: When must you indicate when turning right at a roundabout?
A: Only signal right as you approach the roundabout.
B: Signal right all through the roundabout.
C: Signal right when you approach the roundabout, then signal left as you pass the exit before the one you wish to take.
D: Don’t signal, take the first gap.
Explanation: To turn right at a roundabout, signal right as you approach. As you pass the exit before the one you want, switch to a left signal to show you're leaving.

Question: What must you do before going over a rail crossing?
A: Speed up to beat the train.
B: Drive on an angle to lessen the bumps.
C: Search up and down the railway line and check there is space on the other side to exit.
D: Stop at every railway line.
Explanation: Before crossing a railway line, look up and down the line for trains and make sure there's room for your whole vehicle on the other side, so you can't get stuck on the tracks.

Question: What would usually happen if your front left tyre blows out?
A: The car will come to an immediate stop.
B: The rear will sway from side to side.
C: The car will pull towards the right.
D: The car will pull towards the left.
Explanation: If a front tyre blows out, the vehicle usually pulls towards the side of the blown tyre, here the left. Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator and brake gently.

Question: What would usually happen if you had a left rear tyre blow out?
A: The car will come to an immediate stop.
B: The rear will sway from side to side.
C: The car will pull towards the right.
D: The car will pull towards the left.
Explanation: A rear tyre blowout usually makes the back of the vehicle sway from side to side. Hold the wheel firmly, keep straight, ease off the accelerator and brake gently once you're in control.
